voyage.name: Future Nepal
voyage.content: Future Nepal is a volunteer organization in Nepal established in 2002 and registered with social welfare council of Nepal. It is a non—governmental and extremely non-profitable organization working under the principle of “change society by Volunteering”. It established with the objective of changing and promoting the status of the country through “Volunteering in Nepal”. The members of its group have collected enough

voyage.name: Hidden Journeys Nepal
voyage.content: Organizes tours that take guests to visit and learn from Nepal's change makers, e.g., social entrepreneurs, artists, activists and other innovators. There are prearranged tours (usually 2 days including a networking session in the evening) on specific issues - or you can design your own.

voyage.name: Volunteer Society Nepal
voyage.content: Based in an off-the-beaten-track neighbourhood in southeast Kathmandu, all volunteers are placed in local homestays and have the opportunity to use their skills to give back to the community. Volunteer work is personalised according to your ability, and you’ll be living as a part of the community you are helping. Learn to make momos, speak Nepali, dance, and all about modern Nepali culture from your host family, and

voyage.name: Himalayan Bank
voyage.address: Karmachari Sanchaya Kosh Bldg, Tridevi Sadak

voyage.name: Nepal Rastra Bank, Central Office
voyage.content: Banking Office (address:Thapathali)

voyage.name: Boudha Stupa
voyage.price: Foreigners pay Rs400, but this can be waived for guests of hotels at the other side of the stupa
voyage.content: According to legend, Boudhanath Stupa was built in the 5th century AD by an elderly poultry woman who sought land from the king to construct a shrine to the Buddha. The king agreed, offering her as much land as she could cover with the skin of a water buffalo. Cleverly, she cut the hide into thin strips and laid them end to end, creating a vast circumference. Though the king realized he had been outwitted, he honored

voyage.name: Pashupatinath Temple
voyage.content: This important Hindu temple is dedicated to Shiva in his form as the Lord of the Beasts. While only Hindus are allowed to enter the inner sanctum, the surrounding temple grounds are open to all visitors. The area features not only historic architecture and rich religious iconography, but also sadhus (holy men), a market for spiritual items, and a revered sacred cave. One of the most fascinating parts of the complex i

voyage.name: Taragaon Museum
voyage.content: turn it into a do umentation centre documenting what artists, photographers, architects, anthropologists and Samskritists from abroad had contributed in the second half of the 20th century to identify, highlight and preserve the cultural heritage of the Kathmandu Valley.

voyage.name: Guhyeshwari Temple
voyage.content: One of the Shakti Peethas of Nepal, considered auspicious to Shakti devotees.

voyage.name: Dilyak Dabzang Monastery
voyage.content: The oldest original Karma Kagyu monastery in Boudha, Nepal. The monastery was established by Very Ven. 7th Dabzang Rinpoche year 1963 near the great stupa of Boudha.

voyage.name: Khawalung Monastery
voyage.content: A beautiful Tibetan monastery near Boudhanath Stupa. It is inaugurated by Trulshik Rinpoche and Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche in October 2005. The monastery has an elementary and a training school. It consists of monks from remote region of Nepal and Tibet. There are many exquisite Tibetan Buddhist wall paintings.

voyage.name: Shechen Monastery
voyage.content: A very spacious and beautiful temple founded by the late Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. There is a garden restaurant near the monastery guest house.

voyage.name: Himalayan Singing Bowl Centre
voyage.content: Sells hand-made singing bowls. Singing bowls are a new concept and did not exist in Tibet as instruments of healing

voyage.name: Rokpa
voyage.content: A charity empowering disadvantaged women. Handmade bags and meditation cushions. Products are well made with innovative designs.

voyage.name: Boudha Stupa Restaurant & Cafe
voyage.content: Specializes in Nepali and Tibetan cuisine. Veg & Non-veg meals. Clay oven pizzas. Views over the stupa.

voyage.name: Himalayan Cafe
voyage.content: Clean cafe offering traditional Tibetan & Western breakfast, lunch & dinner. Cafe is above Buddhist shop & is on 3, 4 & 5th floors overlooking the stupa. Excellent veggie burger with fried for Rs120. Small pot of milk tea Rs75. Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Organic Smoothie Bowl and Cafe
voyage.content: Excellent meals prepared with organic ingredients. Sourdough bread. Healthy and tasty smoothies. Polite and quick service. Dull, uninspired interior.

voyage.name: Stupa Dining Restaurant With Garden
voyage.address: Boudha, Dhara Tole, before turning to Hyatt Road
voyage.content: Local restaurant with good, clean, cheap food, and with live music.

voyage.name: Utpala Cafe
voyage.content: Pure vegan restaurant with ethics. Good coffee. Wide range of tasty Indian and Italian dishes. Healthy juices. Reasonable prices. Only outdoor seating in a beer garden-like setting. Good place to grab a meal, but not to relax and hang out.

voyage.name: Cafe Caravan
voyage.content: Excellent coffee and desserts. Western favourites, muesli, French toast, pasta, and local food, momos and thukpa. Cosy interior - a cross between Freak Street and Dolpo. Personalized service from owner. A number of stupa-facing window seats. Highly recommended carrot cake.

voyage.name: Flavors
voyage.content: Tucked away at the end of alley. Outdoor seating only. Good coffee. Excellent food.

voyage.name: Himalayan Java Coffee
voyage.content: Boudha branch of the ubiquitous Himalayan Java chain. Spacious and chic. Small number of seats offering views over the stupa. Excellent coffee.

voyage.name: Kar.ma Coffee
voyage.content: Cosy, elegant cafe. Excellent coffee and cakes. Stylish and earthy handmade cups and coffee-making utensils on sale. Indoor and outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Roadhouse Cafe
voyage.content: Large and spacious with contemporary design. Excellent wood-fired pizza. Rooftop seating. Views over the stupa.

voyage.name: Ugyen Cafe
voyage.content: Elegant cafe inside monastery compound. Large outside seating area, including Zen-style floor space. Excellent coffee and desserts. A number of veggie combo breakfast options. Small selection of Buddhist books and magazines to read on the premise.

voyage.name: Dragon Guesthouse
voyage.content: A pleasant guesthouse with garden, restaurant, and free Wi-Fi. Convenient for Boudha Stupa.

voyage.name: Tharlam GuestHouse
voyage.content: Some of the rooms are nice and clean but the ones downstairs, with kitchen, not so much. They have rats and little cockroaches. It's at the end of a very narrow and dark alley, and there have been lots of robberies at night. Not recommendable. Beside/affiliated with the beautiful Tharlam Sasang Namgyal Ling Monastery. One bedroom for 1 person: Rs400; twin beds or double bed for 2: Rs$800; Suite or bedroom with kitche

voyage.name: Hotel Butsugen
voyage.content: A bright an airy hotel. Close to stupa. Free WIFI. Breakfast included in rates.

voyage.name: Rinchen Hotel
voyage.content: Large rooms. Close to cafes and restaurants. A 2 to 3 minute walk to Boudha Stupa.

voyage.name: Rokpa Guesthouse
voyage.content: A charity run guesthouse. Profits used to support underprivileged youth. Staff are trainees from disadvantaged backgrounds. Cosy rooms. Cafe and restaurant. Garden. Shop selling goods made by women from underprivileged families.

voyage.name: Shechen Guest House
voyage.content: In the grounds of Shechen Monastery in Boudha has clean & good quality rooms with private bathrooms for about USD10 (2011). Guesthouse also has garden with restaurant/coffee shop facilities & is within a five minute walk of Bodhnath Stupa.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Kathmandu
voyage.content: 5 star hotel with 290 rooms and suites. Has a health and beauty spa, swimming pool, wading pool for children and an outdoor whirlpool. 4 km from Tribhuvan International Airport and within walking distance of Baudha Stupa.

voyage.name: J Art Gallery
voyage.content: Displays the artwork of eminent, established Nepalese painters.

voyage.name: Machali Mandir, Teku
voyage.content: A small two storey pagoda

voyage.name: Matrikeshwor Mahadev
voyage.content: Middle of Rani Pokhari Pond

voyage.name: Asa Archives
voyage.content: Specialising in medieval history and religious traditions of the Kathmandu Valley. The archives have a collection of some 6,000 loose-leaf handwritten books and 1,000 palm-leaf manuscripts (mostly in Sanskrit or Nepal Bhasa) and a manuscript dated to 1464.

voyage.name: Narayanhiti Palace Museum
voyage.content: Narayanhiti comes from Narayana, a form of the Hindu god Lord Vishnu, and Hiti, meaning "water spout" (Vishnu's temple is located opposite the palace, and the water spout is located east of the main entrance to the precinct). Narayanhiti was a new palace, in front of the old palace built in 1915, and was built in 1970 in the form of a contemporary Pagoda. It was built on the occasion of the marriage of King Birenda B

voyage.name: NAFA Gallery
voyage.content: This is housed in Sita Bhavan, a neo-classical old Rana palace.

voyage.name: Nepal Art Council Gallery
voyage.content: This gallery contains artwork of both national and international artists and extensive halls regularly used for art exhibitions

voyage.name: Russian Centre of Science and Culture
voyage.alt: Russian: Российский Центр Науки и Культуры
voyage.hours: Office Hours: Mon-Thu 09:00-18:00, Fri 09:00-17:00, Lunch Hours: 14:00-15:00
voyage.address: Pashupati Marga, Block No. 1055/31, Kamal Pokhari

voyage.name: Sankha Park
voyage.content: close to Ring Road

voyage.name: Tribhuvan University Central Library
voyage.content: One of the largest libraries in Nepal situated within Tribhuvan University premise at Kirtipur. You can get there by regular bus or micro-bus for Kirtipur. Has a large collection of old and new books, journals and newspapers.

voyage.name: Mandala Book Point
voyage.content: Kantipath. Probably the best for all types of reference, academic texts, tourist books and maps. Mandala also publishes books on sociology, anthropology, culture, politics and history of Nepal. It also a centre for most scholars visiting Nepal and patrons are encouraged to take part in the lively and informative discussions that frequently occur in the shop in the evening. The most reliable shop for The Economist and

voyage.name: Quixote's Cove: the bookshop
voyage.content: Jawalakhel. Located next to New Orleans Cafe in Jawalakhel, this bookshop is housed in an old 1930s building and combines a great collection of fiction with a marvelously cosy environment.

voyage.name: Bhat Bhateni Shopping Mall
voyage.content: A big Supermarket

voyage.name: City Center Mall
voyage.content: also email ankit@citycentre.com.np A five-storey shopping mall is centrally Air-conditioned. - International Branded Show Rooms - Electronic, Mobile, Camera. - Readymade section - Wedding Floor (Sarees, Ornaments, Boutique, Beauty corner, Palour), - Food Court (Chinese, Korean, Italian, Thai, Japanese, Vietnamese dishes), Gaming zone.

voyage.name: People's Plaza
voyage.content: Electronic Accessories (one shop), Gents Ladies and kids (two shop), Gents Wear (six shops), Ladies Wear (nine shops), Shoe's shop (seven units), Food Court

voyage.name: Irish Pub Lazimpat
voyage.content: Irish dishes, a great variety of beer (also Guinness) and whisky (international and local), Irish Coffee (also Creamy Irish Coffee) cocktails, mocktails, energy cocktails, summer cocktails, shooters (try "Irish Flag"). During the cold season, you can also find "hot winter drinks". Friday nights live music, dart. Well trained, friendly staff. Run under German management.

voyage.name: Hotel Ambassador
voyage.price: NPR2500 Per person in double room
voyage.content: Rooms are good, clean and comfortable, as long as the window does not face the main street. It is about 10 minutes walking from Thamel, so the environment is not as hectic, but the bars are still at a walking distance. It includes unlimited free use of internet in the two computers on the lobby

voyage.name: Dream Nepal Hotel and Apartment
voyage.price: Suite Room Sgl /Dbl: US$ 70/80, Studio Apartment Sgl /Dbl: US$ 80/180, Deluxe Room Sgl /Dbl: US$ 50/60
voyage.address: Amrit Marg, near to Brahmakumari Marg

voyage.name: Dwarika's
voyage.content: A fair four-star hotel with unique charm of old newari palace architecture. Has a swimming pool and the renowned restaurant "Krishnarpan" which serves elaborate multi course Nepali dinner (only on reservation)..

voyage.name: Hotel Hukum Darbar
voyage.price: Standard Room Sgl/Dbl USD 60 / 80, Deluxe Room.Sgl/Dbl USD 80 / 100, Extra bed USD 35 (only in deluxe room), Breakfast / Lunch or Dinner USD 6 / 10

voyage.name: Hotel Soaltee Crowne Plaza
voyage.content: Five star hotel. It also has Al Fresco, the most authentic Italian restaurant in Kathmandu. Although the hotel is rated as a 5 star, it takes a generous person to give it that rating, however that is relative to the other hotels. Double confirm your rooms for preferences (smoking or non-smoking) and do not get a ground floor room.

voyage.name: The Shanker Hotel
voyage.price: Starts at US$80. 20% discount for online bookings
voyage.content: Formerly a Rana palace bought over in 1964. Luxurious 100 year old palace hotel. 4.5 acre property in the heart of the city. A typically Nepali Maharaja's Palace.

voyage.name: Yak and Yeti
voyage.content: A five star hotel located in a converted palace on Durbar Marg. This is a landmark since Nepal first opened to tourism at the end of World War II. At that time the King was living in exile in Calcutta (present-day Kolkata) and was ask to return to govern the nation. He asked Boris Lesonavich, a Russian also in exile to come to Nepal and establish tourist accommodation in Kathmandu. He established the Palace Hotel in

voyage.name: Swayambhunath
voyage.alt: स्वय म्भू AKA the Monkey Temple
voyage.price: Foreigners: Rs200 for single entry; Rs750 for a multiple entry pass
voyage.content: Perched on a hill overlooking Kathmandu, Swayambhu is a revered site featuring a grand stupa surrounded by Buddhist and Hindu iconography. According to legend, a former Buddha visited the valley, which was then a vast lake. The Buddha planted a lotus seed in the clear waters that bloomed after 84,000 years, crowned with an eternal flame. Drawn by the flame from Mount Wutai in China, the bodhisattva Manjushri drained

voyage.name: Freak Street
voyage.content: Historic street where western hippies seeking enlightenment would stay in the 1970s and 80s. Now just a few restaurants and hotels but the iconic Snowman Cafe is tucked away here. Opened in 1965 as a full functioning restaurant, Snowman is now a cafe shop with new Nescafe machine and paper cups, but still run by the same family. Since the family owns the property, this cafe shop survived from the pressure of rent. Ho

voyage.name: Thamel Chowk
voyage.content: A tourist area with many restaurants and shops.

voyage.name: Garden of Dreams
voyage.price: Rs400 for non-Nepalese, Rs150 for Nepalese
voyage.content: Relax in this beautiful and peaceful walled garden close to Thamel and the former Royal Palace. Beautifully renovated in partnership with the Austrian government. It has two pavilions depicting two of the six annual seasons in the Hindu calendar. There is a mini exhibition showing old photos of this garden. There is a restaurant (Kaiser Cafe) in it. You are not allowed to bring own food into the garden and even if yo

voyage.name: Lakhu Phalechā
voyage.content: A roadside shelter is linked with the founding of Nepal Sambat. This is where the porters from Bhaktapur are said to have rested with their loads of sand. The procession of the goddess Dāgin, which is held during the Yenya festival, starts from this house.

voyage.name: Moti Azima Gallery
voyage.content: In a three-story building which contains an impressive collection of traditional utensils and handmade dolls and items typical of a medieval Newar house, giving an important insight into Nepalese history.

voyage.name: Kumari Palace
voyage.content: Home of "the Kumari", or living goddess, a young girl.

voyage.name: Kasthamandap
voyage.alt: Nepali: काष्ठमण्डप Kāṣṭhamaṇḍap, Newar: मरु सत्तल Maru Sattal; literally "Wood-Covered Shelter"
voyage.content: A three-storey temple enshrining an image of Gorakhnath. It was built in the 16th century in pagoda style. The name of Kathmandu is a derivative of the word Kasthamandap. It was built under the reign of King Laxmi Narsingha Malla. It was built as a rest house for travelers.

voyage.name: Nasal Chowk
voyage.content: Statues, temples and the Rana museum in the Hanuman Dhoka former palace complex. The courtyard was used for royal coronations until 2001.

voyage.name: Taleju Temple
voyage.content: One of the oldest temples in the square, this three-roofed temple with its pyramid shaped bases, is an example of the typical Newari architectural style.

voyage.name: Mahendra Museum
voyage.content: This museum is dedicated to King Mahendra of Nepal (1920–1972). It includes his personal belongings such as decorations, stamps, coins and personal notes and manuscripts, but it also has reconstructions of his cabinet room and office chamber.

voyage.name: National Museum
voyage.content: This in an historical building. It was constructed in the early 19th century by General Bhimsen Thapa. It is the most important museum in the country, housing an extensive collection of weapons, art and antiquities of historic and cultural importance. The museum was established in 1928 as a collection house of war trophies and weapons, and the initial name of this museum was Chhauni Silkhana, meaning "the stone house

voyage.name: The Natural History Museum
voyage.alt: Natural Science Museum of Tribhuvan University
voyage.content: This museum has a sizeable collection of different species of animals, butterflies, and plants. The museum is noted for its display of species, from prehistoric shells to stuffed animals.

voyage.name: Royal Mahendra Museum
voyage.price: Entry is free if you have a ticket for the Durbar Square for Rs1000

voyage.name: Museum Of Nepali Art
voyage.content: Mostly paintings by current Nepali artists.

voyage.name: Tribhuvan Museum
voyage.content: contains artifacts related to the King Tribhuvan (1906–1955). It has a variety of pieces including his personal belongings, letters and papers, memorabilia related to events he was involved in and a rare collection of photos and paintings of the Royal family.

voyage.name: Evangelical Ashish Church
voyage.content: The sole church in Kathmandu

voyage.name: Dhansā Degah
voyage.content: A 17th-century pagoda-shaped building. Its carved wood windows provide an example of the art of woodworking which has been highly developed in the Kathmandu Valley since antiquity. The upper part was destroyed in the Great Earthquake of 1934, and its height was shortened when it was repaired. It was built as a courthouse. A shrine to Nāsa Dya, the god of music, exists on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Gakuti
voyage.content: This building is a three-sided courtyard. There is a temple dedicated to Mahadev at the centre.

voyage.name: Ichangu Narayan Temple
voyage.content: The temple contains four representations of the deity Narayan (another name of Vishnu).

voyage.name: The Temple of Maru Ganedya
voyage.content: It is one of the more important Ganesh shrines in Kathmandu. A notable feature of this temple is the absence of the usual pinnacle.

voyage.name: Shantipura Building
voyage.content: Part of the Swayambhunath Complex

voyage.name: Pilgrims Book House
voyage.content: It is the largest and most well-established English language bookshop in Kathmandu. They have great sections on Buddhism, including a whole room devoted to Vajrayana, as well as an encyclopedic selection on books devoted to subjects on Nepal.

voyage.name: Tibet Book Store
voyage.content: Great selection of books on all subjects, but specializes in books on Buddhism and Tibet studies.

voyage.name: Vajra Books
voyage.content: Has huge selection of books on Buddhism, Nepal and Tibet studies.

voyage.name: Gupta
voyage.content: A local restaurant that serves South Indian snacks, Indian dishes, and traditional Indian desserts. It is clean, has friendly staff and is very cheap.

voyage.name: Helena's Rooftop Restaurant
voyage.price: chicken tikka masala costs around Rs350
voyage.content: Excellent food, great service, and modest prices. It is claimed to have the tallest rooftop restaurant in Kathmandu, and the views from there of the city, especially at night, are reported to be worth the climb. Serves Western and regional cuisine.

voyage.name: New Orleans
voyage.content: A good variety of well-made food, including pasta, Nepali and salads. Pleasant Newari courtyard setting

voyage.name: Northfield Cafe
voyage.content: Basic pub grub and Nepali attempt at Mexican, often with live traditional music. Popular with English teachers and expats.

voyage.name: OR2K
voyage.content: It is Israeli-run and has a wide variety of good, safe vegetarian food, especially good if you are craving a salad.

voyage.name: Roadhouse Cafe
voyage.content: Excellent wood fired pizza. Pleasant decor with good coffee & hot chocolate & more cappuccinos. Draught Everest beer, when available. A relaxing, upscale place for when you need to escape from Kathmandu for an evening. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Rum Doodle
voyage.content: Excellent food at modest prices, including live music on most nights. Carry on straight past Helena's, around the "chicane", where the road bends then straightens out again, and turn the next right. It is signposted but the sign's fairly small. Everest summiteers can eat here for free. Extraphone=+977-1-4248692

voyage.name: Thamel House Restaurant
voyage.content: Nepali and Newari cuisine. There is a cultural show every evening from 19:00.

voyage.name: Chikusa Café
voyage.content: Nepali coffee, milk tea, sandwiches and crêpes. Strawberry lassi is a speciality. Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Gaia Restaurant and Coffee Shop
voyage.content: Good selection of coffees and teas. Pleasant outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Mitho
voyage.content: A cosy cafe with a long history in Thamel. Excellent and healthy meals. Good coffee.

voyage.name: Falcha Cafe
voyage.content: Warm, cosy environment. Views over Freak Street. Good coffee. Very reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Kafemandu
voyage.content: Excellent coffee. Good quality international cuisine. Stylish interior. Very friendly and helpful service.

voyage.name: Irish Pub Lazimpat
voyage.content: Irish dishes, a great variety of beer (also Guinness) and whisky (international and local), Irish Coffee (also Creamy Irish Coffee) cocktails, mocktails, energy cocktails, summer cocktails, shooters (try "Irish Flag"). During the cold season, you can also find "hot winter drinks". Friday nights live music, dart. Well trained, friendly staff. Run under German management.

voyage.name: Jessy Penny
voyage.content: A nice bar in Freak Street on several floors. Each floor has its own atmosphere. It is also possible to have shishas at the first floor.

voyage.name: Alobar1000
voyage.price: Dorm bed: Rs300; Private room Rs1,500
voyage.content: Two beautifully designed homes with a bar, cozy lounge area, weight room, movie hall, dining hall and communal kitchen. They also have 24-hr hot shower. The staff treat you like family, and the owners, brothers Shiva and Tashi, are generous hosts (Shiva is a fantastic cook). There's also a guard at the door, free and strong Wi-Fi and people congregate on the roftop lounge nightly.

voyage.name: Avalon House
voyage.content: Nice ensuite rooms with small TV, Wi-Fi, nice roof terrace. Solar powered batteries for some lights and Wi-Fi during power outages. Breakfast included.

voyage.name: Chillout Resort
voyage.content: It has a nice rooftop garden restaurant with good food and helpful staff. Rooms with clean private bathrooms that have hot/cold showers. There's also free Wi-Fi in rooms, restaurant and lobby. Airport pick-up and drop-off.

voyage.name: Hotel Ashoka
voyage.content: 3 beds, 4 beds in a room available and suitable for families, bigger groups & large families on budget. A diner, bar, laundry, barber, provision store are nearby, and it is easy walking distance to Ratna Park for trips.

voyage.name: Hotel Backpackers Inn
voyage.content: Every room has cable TV and 24-hour hot and cold showers. Nepalese, Chinese, Indian and Continental cuisines available.

voyage.name: Big Tree Hostel
voyage.price: Dorms from Rs500, private rooms from Rs600
voyage.address: on Pipalbote Marg, at the square with the holy tree
voyage.content: Very cozy hostel in the northwestern part of Thamel. Great outdoor common areas including rooftop and yoga space. Hot water around the clock, the facilities are rather basic and regularly cleaned. Very helpful staff when it comes to trekking in Nepal. Also has a great selection of trekking maps that can be borrowed at the reception.

voyage.name: Hotel Blue Horizon
voyage.content: Friendly staff, and good room service breakfasts.

voyage.name: Hotel Down Town
voyage.content: Surrounded by dance bars, but nice rooftop and rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel Impala Garden
voyage.content: Budget accommodation in Thamel!

voyage.name: Hotel Travelers Home
voyage.content: Nice hotel.

voyage.name: Kathmandu Peace Guesthouse
voyage.content: Not to be mistaken for the pricier and up-scale, but not so peaceful name brother, Kathmandu Guesthouse. In a more peaceful area just outside Thamel.

voyage.name: King's Land
voyage.content: Family-run hotel. The owner and his wife are very friendly and helpful. The rooms are old but clean. Wifi, hot water, roof top available.

voyage.name: Lhasa Guest House
voyage.content: Very friendly and helpful staff, lived in Kathmandu all their lives, rooms are large, clean, and have hot water when power is on. Rooms cost from Rs300. Double for Rs800. Has free bag storage while you go on a trek, so long as you spend a night or two. The best thing is the free Wi-Fi that doesn't shut off even when the power goes down.

voyage.name: Millennium Guest House
voyage.content: Decent cheap guesthouse just outside Thamel, quiet area, nice terrace.

voyage.name: Nirvana Peace Home
voyage.content: Paknajol, near Thamel.

voyage.name: Shangrila Guest House
voyage.content: Fun and friendly guest house on the edge of Thamel but with dubious business practices and not particularly clean. Water was orange colour and no hot water.

voyage.name: Sparkling Turtle Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: Outside of Thamel, near the Swayambunath (Monkey) Temple, this place is quiet, full of backpackers, and serves incredible food. Rs300/night including breakfast. Free Wi-Fi, cool roof terrace, bar, Canadian managed. Impossible to find as they don't really advertise. Get a taxi or walk to Buddha Park near Swayambunath and call (+977 1 428 4647) from there, they'll come pick you up.

voyage.name: Student Guest House
voyage.content: Friendly staff who will always try to help you out. On the edge of Thamel, easy to find. Internet is available at the entrance as well as a laundry service.

voyage.name: Sun Rise Cottage
voyage.content: Nice family run guesthouse in a quiet street just south of central Thamel, lovely big rooms, simple furnishings, clean and with hot water 24 hr. Great garden area to relax and friendly family.

voyage.name: Hotel Encounter Nepal
voyage.content: In the north Thamel (about 20 m down from the Map of Thamel), 4 minutes' walk from the centre of Thamel. Clean, peaceful place with free Wifi, computers, garden restaurant & friendly staff. In the hotel there is also the office of Alpine Club of Himalaya, where you can book tours, etc. Rooms rates begin at US$15.

voyage.name: Hotel Ganesh Himal
voyage.content: Decent rooms and good service. Hot water, TV and hot food. Quieter location in Chhetrapati Chowk, great views and balconies.

voyage.name: Hotel Harati
voyage.content: Located on the main street from/through Thamel into Durbar Square (which is about 5-10 minutes away on foot, or a Rs50 rickshaw or taxi ride). Clean, hygienic and comfortable rooms, including en-suites with hot showers most of the time. The website quotes rooms from US$75, but this is negotiable.

voyage.name: Mi Casa Hotel
voyage.content: 24-hour front desk and room service, daily housekeeping, private bathroom for each unit, safe, luggage storage, free wireless internet service. Laundry and dry cleaning service. Air conditioning and heating. Cable TV. Baby-sitting service. Doctor on call. Airport transfer (free airport pick up). Tour desk

voyage.name: Kathmandu Guest House
voyage.content: Thamel. The original guesthouse now with rooms ranging from basic to almost-fancy. Restaurant and bar. The axis on the compass of Thamel, all other addresses are given in relation to this hotel. Rates US$8-160. Wi-Fi internet access (semi-reliable) from lobby, garden and some rooms for Rs75/hr. Otherwise, 4 computers with internet access until midnight, Rs60/hour. The guest house has a sister concern in Pokhara.

voyage.name: Hotel Utse
voyage.content: The hotel has a quaint and homely Tibetan theme and rooms are also clean, hygienic and comfortable. The hotel has a restaurant on the ground floor that serves Tibetan/Chinese/Continental cuisine (open 06:00 to 22:00), in addition to a rooftop terrace. There are standard/deluxe/super deluxe rooms US$15 - 35. Deluxe rooms include attached shower/bath with 24-hr hot water and cable TV. Good value.

voyage.name: Tibet Guest House
voyage.content: Thamel. Operating 1984 has rooms 102. 24 hours room service, free Wi-Fi,coffee shop, beauty parlour and travel desk. Rate US$16-96.

voyage.name: Sacred Valley Inn - Kathmandu
voyage.content: Lovely rooms in this clean, comfortable hotel in Thamel. Great location. Good rooftop area to sit and relax and eat. Simple but delicious food served in the restaurant. Helpful and knowledgeable staff.

voyage.name: Kathmandu Sunny Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel claims it is designed to be 100% earthquake-resistant. Far from the busy roads, the atmosphere is quiet and peaceful.

voyage.name: Institute of Natural Medicine
voyage.content: A mid-range accommodation with Yoga and Retreat, Massage, Sound Healing service as well as training programs.

voyage.name: Shangri-La Hotel
voyage.price: Deluxe room/Executive club room/ Junior suite room UUSD105 / 120 / 210
voyage.content: Inclusive breakfast & airport pick up. Room service. A comfortable seating area and cable TV are included and all rooms are fully air-conditioned. Free Wi-Fi. Massage option at the spa. 24 hour concierge.
